title: A Whole-of-society Approach Towards Addressing Discrimination
what_it_is: A Whole-of-society Approach Towards Addressing Discrimination

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Bill debate
sections.summary: Last month the House debated the Workplace Fairness Bill, which legislated against workplace discrimination through 11 protected characteristics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last month, we debated in this House on the Workplace Fairness Bill where we legislated against discrimination at the workplace through 11 protected characteristics.

sections.label: Five ways against discrimination
sections.summary: Discrimination work is a work in progress, and five ways are offered, starting with anti-discrimination work in schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It remains a work in progress and something we certainly cannot take for granted or leave to chance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I offer five ways for us to consider in addressing discrimination as part of our forward-looking aspiration as a young nation that espouses justice and equality as deep rooted values in our national pledge, no less.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, it is important that our work against discrimination starts young and in our schools.

sections.label: Goh Chok Tong Enable Awards
sections.summary: Recipients of the Goh Chok Tong Enable Awards, including an architect, a chef and a banker, achieved much despite disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, in the area of disabilities, when we hear of the incredible stories and achievements of those awarded the Goh Chok Tong Enable Awards over the years, one cannot help but be inspired by what these individuals have achieved in spite of their life challenges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Among the prior recipients are an architect with projects not just in Singapore but in China, India and the Middle East, a chef at a Michelin star restaurant and a banker, all of whom struggle with some form of disability but have achieved much the same, if not more, than many of us.

sections.label: Insurance, review and Government leadership
sections.summary: It asks whether insurance criteria assess disabled and mentally ill individuals fairly, urges review of legislative positions, and calls on Government to lead.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In relation to refusal, loading and exclusionary criteria for insurance plans, are individuals with specific disability and mental health conditions assessed fairly or are there instances where decisions are taken too conservatively such that insurance coverage is unfairly onerous or even impossible?

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It needs to be the case that if we are serious about eroding discriminatory practices, we should continue to review and be ever circumspect about our legislative positions and policy frameworks to encourage systemic parity and fair access, especially for marginalised groups.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My fifth and final point, Mr Speaker, is a call for the Government, being the largest employer in Singapore today and one that permeates influence in a variety of sectors relating to society, to take the lead in challenging discriminatory narratives and for itself to shape positive ones proactively, simply because it has the remit, scale and opportunity to do so.

sections.label: National Service for amputees
sections.summary: It asks whether National Service could be possible for a male amputee or person with disability able to serve in a non-combat role.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, if we consider that the Government has shifted to be more inclusive now in all of its functions, could it potentially mean that National Service, as an example, would be possible for a male amputee or one with a disability but who is otherwise well, functional and able to serve the country in a non-combat role?

sections.label: Biases, discrimination and three pillars
sections.summary: Using a painting analogy, it urges Members to consider their biases and blind spots, and states an approach anchored on three pillars.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If paintings were all made with a very broad stroke of one colour, little tone and no texture, and we make a harsh assumption that all other forms did not, could not or must not fit into the painting, we allow discrimination to take hold and prevent us from adding colour to our lives and from making it more beautiful and enriching for ourselves and for the people around us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge all Members of the House to consider how we form our biases today and where our blind spots could be in hope that we could work together towards eradicating all manner of discrimination, whether they be in the corridors of our Housing and Development Board flats and our homes, at work in our offices, among students in our classrooms or just in our everyday conversations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Our approach is anchored on three pillars: first, legislative safeguards to combat discrimination; second, policies that foster social integration and protect the interests of minorities; and third, enlarging our common spaces.

sections.label: Compulsory Education and Workplace Fairness
sections.summary: The Compulsory Education Act was amended in 2016 for students with disabilities, and the Workplace Fairness Bill was passed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For instance, we amended the Compulsory Education Act in 2016 to ensure that students with disabilities, including those with moderate to severe special educational needs, have access to education.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We recently strengthened our legal framework to prevent discrimination in the workplace with the passing of the Workplace Fairness Bill.

sections.label: School SEN Support and Disability Sports
sections.summary: Schools have peer support networks for students with SEN, and by 2028 all schools will conduct at least one disability sports-related programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For instance, schools have peer support networks to support students with SEN, and by 2028 all schools will conduct at least one disability sports-related programme.

sections.label: SG Enable Hubs and Beyond the Label
sections.summary: SG Enable is piloting Enabling Services Hubs, and Beyond the Label is the National Council of Social Service's public education campaign on mental health.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: SG Enable is also piloting the Enabling Services Hubs to build inclusive communities where persons with disabilities and their caregivers can be an integral part of the communities in which they live. “Beyond the Label” is the National Council of Social Service's public education campaign that seeks to normalise conversations around mental health and promote social inclusion for persons with mental health conditions.

sections.label: Disability Sports Master Plan and ArtsEverywhere
sections.summary: Ten strategic moves were announced under the Disability Sports Master Plan 2024, and ArtsEverywhere@CDC was launched to bring arts to the heartlands.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Last year, we announced 10 strategic moves under the Disability Sports Master Plan 2024, to engage, enrich and further empower persons with disabilities through sports.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Last year, the National Arts Council and People’s Association launched ArtsEverywhere@CDC programme to bring the arts closer to the heartlands.
